title: BenevolentAI knowledge graph proposed baricitinib for COVID-19; randomized trials and regulators confirmed benefit
summary: AI knowledge graph proposed baricitinib in Feb 2020; ACTT-2 showed faster recovery and COV-BARRIER lower 28-day mortality (a secondary endpoint); FDA and WHO endorsed it.
account: On 4 February 2020 BenevolentAI staff published a Lancet correspondence. It reported that the company's machine-learning-built knowledge graph identified baricitinib, a rheumatoid-arthritis JAK inhibitor, as a candidate against 2019-nCoV because it binds AAK1. AAK1 is a regulator of viral endocytosis. Randomized trials tested it. ACTT-2 (1,033 patients, enrolled 8 May to 1 July 2020) reported median recovery of 7 days versus 8 (rate ratio 1.16, 95% CI 1.01–1.32). On high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation, 10 versus 18 days. COV-BARRIER (1,525 patients) missed its primary endpoint of disease progression (27.8% versus 30.5%, odds ratio 0.85, p=0.18). Its 28-day all-cause mortality, a secondary endpoint, was 8% versus 13% (hazard ratio 0.57, nominal p=0.0018). The Food and Drug Administration (FDA) authorized it with remdesivir on 19 November 2020. WHO strongly recommended it on 14 January 2022.
purpose: Drug repurposing: mine a machine-learning-built biomedical knowledge graph for approved drugs that might block a new coronavirus.
system: BenevolentAI knowledge graph (relationships extracted from literature by machine learning) with AAK1 inhibitor screening
deployer: ACTT-2 Study Group (NIAID); COV-BARRIER investigators (Eli Lilly)
segment: Hospitalized COVID-19 patients requiring supplemental oxygen or ventilatory support
taxonomy_note: The AI's part was candidate identification; the realized good is faster recovery and lower mortality in trials.

ratings.reason: COV-BARRIER reported 28-day all-cause mortality of 8% (62 patients) on baricitinib versus 13% (100 patients) on placebo, hazard ratio 0.57. The randomized comparison supports a life-preserving treatment benefit.
ACTT-2 showed median recovery falling from 8 to 7 days overall and from 18 to 10 days on high-flow oxygen or non-invasive ventilation. That materially eased hospital burden.
WHO strongly recommended baricitinib for severe or critical COVID-19 on 14 January 2022. That made the AI-proposed drug part of standard pandemic care at population scale.

ai_role.statement: The AI's role was hypothesis generation only: BenevolentAI's knowledge graph ranked baricitinib among six high-affinity AAK1-binding approved drugs and the authors published the prediction. It did not design, run or analyze the trials. The demonstrated clinical benefit was established by randomized controlled trials (ACTT-2, COV-BARRIER) conducted by investigators unconnected to BenevolentAI, and judged by FDA and WHO.
